verdicts.strongest_argument: Every hard fact in this claim checks out in primary sources, and every one of them is public. The CFO quote is verbatim in the 2026-06-08 transcript, which was republished the same day by Motley Fool, Investing.com, The Globe and Mail, Yahoo and AOL, and Investing.com's own summary carried the refund-exclusion at summary level. The arithmetic is right: 38.0M shares x $3.62 = $137.6M, so $12M is 8.7% of cap and $0.316/share, and the sole estimate really is $(0.05). The peer-timing premise is also right and is not obscure -- it is the dominant US retail earnings story of the season. SCOTUS voided the IEEPA tariffs 2026-02-20, CBP opened the CAPE refund portal 2026-04-20, and by Q2 prints Target ($994M), Home Depot ($730M), Williams-Sonoma ($167.8M to COGS), Kohl's (~$150M), Abercrombie (~$100M), Columbia ($78M), YETI ($45.6M) and Bob's ($45.1M) had all booked them, in Fortune, Chain Store Age, WWD and Yahoo Finance. Coresight published a gated piece on 2026-08-27 built on precisely this claim's analytical frame -- 'which retailers and brands are excluding potential future tariff refunds from guidance, leaving the benefits as potential upside?' -- six days before this print. And the price did move on the day the fact became known: DLTH rose 29.82% on 2026-06-08. What is genuinely not out is the join: no DLTH-specific piece I could find sizes the $12M against the market cap, against the $28-32M FY EBITDA guide, or against the $(0.05) estimate, and Coresight does not cover the name. So the fact is published in mainstream aggregator copy and the frame is published in sector research; only the magnitude and the this-quarter inference are undrawn. That is a contested-magnitude 45, not a 20 and not an 85. Two real magnitude offsets keep it from going higher on my side of the argument rather than lower: peers routed only ~79-84% of receipts to earnings (Columbia $78M -> $62M; Bob's $45.1M -> $37.9M COGS + $5.7M inventory + $1.5M interest), and Duluth may elect to exclude a one-time duty credit from the adjusted-EBITDA metric it guides on, in which case the headline the market trades tomorrow carries it at zero exactly as the guide does.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Carries the CFO quote verbatim: ~$12M of IEEPA tariffs paid last year, refunds applied for, no benefit included in Q1 results or full-year guidance.
Same-day mainstream summary stating Duluth applied for refunds on ~$12M of IEEPA tariffs and included no benefit in results or FY guidance, alongside the raise to $28-32M adjusted EBITDA.

Sector research whose stated purpose includes identifying which retailers are excluding future tariff refunds from guidance and leaving them as upside -- this claim's exact frame, published six days pre-print, though it does not name Duluth.
Target's Q2 beat driven by a ~$994M IEEPA refund, front-page evidence that the refund-in-Q2 mechanism was common knowledge before this print.

SCOTUS voided IEEPA tariffs 2026-02-20 and CBP activated phase one of the refund process via the CAPE portal on 2026-04-20, i.e. the refund window opened three-plus months before Duluth's 2026-08-02 quarter end.

Bob's Discount Furniture 8-K: $45.1M of IEEPA refunds approved in Q2 2026, split $37.9M to cost of sales, $5.7M to inventory, $1.5M interest income -- the primary-filing template for how much of a receipt actually reaches earnings.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Cuts both ways and I will not overclaim it. Against pricing: the tape into the print is -13.40% over 20 days and -4.23% over 5 days, i.e. DLTH faded straight through the Aug 20 Target and late-August Kohl's refund headlines, which is not the tape of a market marking up a coming $0.32/share windfall; and there is no chain, one estimate, and 46,449 shares/day of volume, so no arbitrage mechanism exists. For pricing: the price did move violently on the date the fact became known -- +29.82% on 2026-06-08 -- and I cannot separate the refund disclosure from the same day's Q1 beat and the raise from $26-30M to $28-32M, which is precisely why this is not a low number. The baseline itself states priced_direction_available is false, so no directional appeal is available to either side.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A DLTH-specific sell-side note, 8-K, or press item between 2026-06-09 and 2026-09-03 that sizes the $12M as per-share upside would take this to 75+; conversely, evidence that Duluth's refund was still unapproved at 2026-08-02 (pushing recognition to Q3) or that it will be excluded from adjusted EBITDA would leave the claim unpriced but strip most of its size.

interactions: Only one finding, so no cross-finding contradiction. Worth flagging for the caller that the finding's novelty and the baseline's largest recent move rest on the same document: the 2026-06-08 Q1 call that produced the $12M refund disclosure also produced the Q1 beat and the raise to $28-32M adjusted EBITDA, and the stock closed +29.82% that day. Any assessment that treats the disclosure as unpriced must accept that the only day it could have been priced is a day the stock rose 30%, and that the attribution between the three items on that call is not separable from public data.
